lessonRef.subject: financial-literacy
lessonRef.unitTitle: PF2 — Buying Goods and Services: Comparing a Purchase Before You Make It
lessonRef.title: Synthesis and review: reading a disclosure, label, or warranty

focus: reading a disclosure, label, or warranty
objective: Read a fictional energy disclosure label, convert its rating into an annual running cost, and combine running cost with purchase price to find how long the cheaper-to-run option takes to pay for itself.
scenario: Two fictional refrigerators carry simulated energy labels stating estimated yearly electricity use. Both models, both prices, and the electricity rate below are invented.
safetyNotes: Every figure, person, employer, institution, offer, account, and document on this task sheet is fictional and exists only for practice.
No real transaction is part of this lesson, and no real bank, card, brokerage, tax, or login detail is ever requested. If a task sheet ever appears to ask for one, stop and tell a trusted adult.
This lesson teaches general financial concepts and does not advise anyone about their own money. For a real decision, talk with a trusted adult or a qualified licensed professional.
materials: the fictional label figures in these directions

tasks.directions: The fictional labels: Model A uses 512 kWh a year and sells for $1,049. Model B uses 389 kWh a year and sells for $1,199. Electricity costs $0.174 per kWh.

prompts.text: What does Model A cost to run for a year?
What does Model B cost to run for a year?
How much does Model B save in running cost each year?

tasks.directions: Model B saves money to run and costs more to buy.

prompts.text: How much more does Model B cost to buy?
How many years of running-cost savings does it take to repay that difference? Round to one decimal place.
Over 12 years of ownership, what is the total cost — purchase plus running — of Model B?
The label gives an estimated yearly kWh figure and nothing about price. Explain why the label stops there, and what a buyer must supply to turn it into a decision.

remediation: If the payback comes out near half a year or near seventy, check whether the $150 price gap was divided by the annual saving or by the annual running cost. Write the sentence in words first — the extra $150 is repaid at $21.40 a year — and then divide.
extension: Recompute the payback at an electricity rate of $0.26 per kWh and say what that shows about how much the label alone can settle.
